_notes: Active-learning ensemble-member learning config, adapting PANAMA's
default_config_files/learning/active_learning_LSTM.json (arXiv 2509.26564v1):
150 epochs (raised from PANAMA's 50: this tiny proxy needs a few thousand gradient updates
to fit, and update count -- steps/epoch x epochs -- is what limits convergence here). Used by
scripts/active_learn.py / nam.train.active_learning.train_ensemble to train each of the 4
disposable ConcatLSTM members serially on one device.
DEVIATIONS from PANAMA (intentional, for this single-GPU port):
* trainer.accelerator is rewritten at runtime to cuda > mps > cpu, so this stays device-agnostic
regardless of the value below.
* PANAMA disables in-loop validation (check_val_every_n_epoch 51) and takes the last checkpoint.
Our train_ensemble selects the val_loss-monitored BEST checkpoint, so validation must run:
check_val_every_n_epoch is left at its default (1) and the data config keeps a validation split.
* batch_size is 32, not PANAMA's 512. Size the batch for MANY optimizer steps per epoch
(~train_windows / 30), NOT to fill memory: this proxy is limited by gradient-update count, and
a memory-filling batch collapses a small round-0 set to a handful of steps/epoch so it never
fits. The capture-app runner (nam.capture.al_runner.compute_al_batch_size) picks the batch this
way automatically; keep it small here for a small set. ConcatLSTM trains with full
backprop-through-time over each ny-length window (train_truncate null), so peak memory scales
with batch_size * ny; ny=32768 (above the loss mask_first, below one LSTM block; see the data
config). batch_size 32 peaks near 5 GiB on MPS -- memory is only an upper bound on the batch,
not the target. If you raise it, also raise the lr (sqrt-scaled) and watch tensorboard to
verify convergence.
* val_dataloader.batch_size is LARGER than train (memory-bounded, not step-bounded): validation
does no backprop, and ESR is a ratio, so a per-batch ESR averaged over many small batches is
not the whole-set ESR -- validation should run in as few batches as possible (ideally one) so
val_loss and best-checkpoint selection are stable. The validation set is fixed-size, so a big
batch just covers it in one pass.
Plain shuffled DataLoader (no capture-grouped batch sampler) is used.
